listNote: Official list as Exophase and PSNProfiles published it before this guide was written; the two agree on every name, description and grade. 55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze.

own.label: Our own advice, from the official description — not yet checked in the game

title: Sunset Platinum — GTA VI Trophy Guide & Tracker

trophies.guide: The platinum. It unlocks itself the moment the other 54 trophies are earned, so there is nothing to do for it directly — it is the receipt for everything else in this guide. Work the roadmap in order: story first, then strangers and activities, then collectibles, chaos and money, and finish with the 100% completion clean-up. When this one pops, the ledger is closed.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Finish the mission Gone Fishing. It comes early in the story, so play the opening missions in order and this one arrives on its own. Free-roam fishing is practice, not the trophy: the pop is tied to completing the mission itself.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1. Story chapters cannot be missed — keep playing the story missions as they appear and the chapter trophy pops at the last one. Use the chapter break as a natural pause point: before moving on, tick off any activities or collectibles you passed, since the next chapter moves the story forward.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2. Like the other chapter trophies it is unmissable and comes from playing the story through in order. Chapter 2 is a good time to start the longer grinds in the background — stunts, vehicles and races all count toward later trophies while you travel between missions.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3. It pops at the chapter's final mission, so there is no separate task — just keep the story moving. By this point the stranger strands and side activities should be opening up; starting them now spreads the work instead of leaving it all for after the finale.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4, the last chapter before the finale. Before you push into the final mission, check the missables page of this guide: the moment and choice trophies cluster around the late story, so this is the last comfortable point to make sure none of them has passed you by. The chapter trophy itself is unmissable.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Finish the final mission of the story. It is the gold bookend to the four chapter trophies and pops when the credits roll on the finale. Do not rush to it: the 100% completion trophy and most of the grind trophies are easier to finish after the story, when the whole map and all activities are open, so treat the finale as the end of stage one, not the end of the run.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Breakfast Run. Named story missions like this one pop their trophy on completion, so play the mission through to its end screen. The official description names the mission but not where it sits in the story, so this guide does not guess its chapter — follow the story markers and it will come to you.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the mission The Cartel Heist. Heist missions in GTA games usually have a setup phase first, so expect preparation missions before the heist itself unlocks — the trophy pops when the heist mission completes. The official description gives the mission name only, so no step-by-step is claimed here; play it as the story presents it.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Child's Play. It is a story mission trophy: finish the mission and the trophy follows. The name suggests family business rather than a heist, so expect story and character work over a set-piece — but that is a reading of the title, not a verified fact, and the description itself names only the mission.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Headliners. Finish the mission and the trophy pops — nothing extra to collect or do on the side. The description names the mission and nothing else, so this guide claims no location, approach or loadout for it; it arrives in the natural course of the story.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the mission VCIA Takedown. VCIA is the Vice City airport, so expect the mission to take you there — but the description names only the mission, so treat the airport as a strong hint from the name, not a confirmed fact. Finish the mission and the trophy pops. It pairs naturally with Catch Me If You Can, the other VCIA trophy, so keep that one in mind while you are at the airport.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the mission Operation Savage Glory. The operation-style name suggests a bigger set-piece mission, but the official description names only the mission — no location or tactic is claimed here. Play the story through and it pops on completion, like the other named-mission trophies.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion on the in-game stats screen (PSN tracks it as 0/100). This is the gold gate before the platinum: it folds in the story, the stranger strands, the activities and the collectibles, so it is really a summary of the whole roadmap rather than a separate task. Leave it for last — chase every other trophy first, then open the stats screen, see what percentage is still missing, and clear exactly that. No single missing item is named by the description, so check the in-game checklist for what counts.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts (PSN tracks 0/250). Stunts are the jumps, airtime and near-miss driving feats the game counts as you drive — the number is large, so do not grind it in one sitting. Instead, drive fast and take jumps whenever you travel between missions and activities, and let the count climb in the background. The description does not define exactly which feats count as a stunt, so watch the in-game counter after a jump to learn what registers.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once (PSN tracks 0/9). This is the sampler trophy: one go at everything — racing, fishing, the shooting range, drone races, the arcade, meditation and the rest — rather than mastery of any of them. Work through the activities list early, tick each type off here as you try it, and the trophy pops on the ninth. The description does not list the nine types, so use the in-game activities menu as the authority on what counts.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges (PSN tracks 0/42). Take the challenges one weapon at a time and repeat any that fall short of gold — the range lets you retry, so a silver or bronze is a practice run, not a failure. Gold medals usually reward accuracy and speed over spray-and-pray, so slow down, aim for the high-value targets first and learn each challenge's layout before chasing the clock. The description does not name the range's location, so this guide does not pin it down.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every one of the 14 locations (PSN tracks 0/14). Visit each drone race spot, win the race there, and tick the location off here — the trophy needs a win everywhere, not just one win. Drone racing rewards clean lines through the gates over raw speed, so learn a course's gate order on a first run and push on the second. The description does not list the 14 locations, so find them in-game and mark each as you win it.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races (PSN tracks 0/20). Different is the key word: winning the same race twenty times does not count — you need twenty distinct race events. Work through the race list across the map, mixing car, bike and whatever other classes the game offers, and tick each new win off here. Races you lose still teach you the course, so retry a lost one immediately while the layout is fresh.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a named rival, so this is a head-to-head: find the fishing challenge against him and out-fish him rather than fishing alone. Fishing challenges usually reward the bigger catch or the higher total, so watch what the challenge actually scores before you cast — the description does not say. The early-game earn rate for this trophy is high (it was one of the first trophies players unlocked), so do it when the fishing challenge first appears.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. Any arcade game counts — pick the shortest one you can find, learn its rules in a practice run, then play it through to completion. It pairs naturally with Master of None, since the arcade is one of the activity types that trophy wants you to try. The description does not name which arcade games exist, so use the in-game arcade list.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete Andy's final mission — the last job in his stranger strand. Stranger strands are chains of side missions: keep answering Andy's calls and following his markers until the strand ends, and this trophy pops at its finale. Do the strands as they appear rather than saving them all for after the story, so the work spreads out. The description names Andy but not where he is found, so this guide does not pin down his location.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's final mission, the end of his stranger strand. Like the other stranger finals, it pops when the last mission in the chain completes — follow Kenton's strand to its end and do not leave a half-finished strand hanging, since a strand's later missions may only unlock after earlier ones are done. The description names Kenton only, so no meeting place is claimed here.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's final mission, the last job of his stranger strand. Stranger strands build toward a finale, so the way to this trophy is simply to keep doing Billy's missions whenever they appear until the strand closes. The description gives Billy's name and nothing else — no location, no mission details — so this guide claims none.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full stranger mission strands (PSN tracks 0/8). This is the silver summary of the stranger system: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone and the other strangers each have a chain, and eight chains must be finished end to end. Start strands early and finish each one before moving on, so you always know which are done — this tracker marks each strand's finale as you earn it. The description does not list the strangers, so the in-game map is the authority on who is still waiting.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's final mission, the last job in his stranger strand. Follow Randy's chain to its end — each mission in a strand unlocks the next, so a strand left half-done is a trophy left half-done. The description names Randy and nothing else, so this guide does not claim where he is or what his missions ask.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's final mission, the last job in his stranger strand. As with the other stranger finals, the route is the strand itself: do Tyrone's missions in order until the chain closes and the trophy pops at the finale. The description names Tyrone only, so no location or mission detail is claimed here.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every one of the 18 meditation spots (PSN tracks 0/18). Meditation spots are quiet places scattered across the state — visit each, meditate there, and tick it off here. Do them while you travel for other trophies, since backtracking across Leonida for a single spot is the slow way. The description does not list the 18 spots, so this guide does not guess them; the in-game map is the source to follow.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Unique means one specific creature, not just any animal — Bret's strand will point you at it, so follow his missions until the hunt itself is offered. Bring a suitable weapon and approach quietly: a unique animal is likely to flee or be lost if spooked, and the description does not say whether the hunt can be retried. Do it when Bret offers it, and do not leave it for later.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets (PSN tracks 0/3). Cards are scattered across Leonida, so this is a collection hunt: pick up cards whenever you pass them and keep a running count per set here. Finish one set completely before chasing the next, and check the in-game collection screen to see which cards of a set are still missing. The description does not say how many cards a set holds or where they are, so this guide claims no locations — collect as you explore.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: WAiNK It at 100 locations (PSN tracks 0/100). WAiNK is the in-game social or camera feature — the count is high, so build the habit early: use it at every new place you visit instead of saving it for a dedicated grind. A hundred locations means the whole map, so pair it with exploring Leonida for The Goodtime State and discovering vehicles for Whip It Good. The description does not define what counts as a location, so watch the counter as you go.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges (PSN tracks 0/50). Challenges are the game's assorted side goals — driving feats, combat feats, exploration and more — and fifty of them must be ticked off. The fastest route is breadth: try a little of everything instead of grinding one kind, and open the challenges menu regularly to see which ones are nearly done. The description does not list the challenges, so the in-game menu is the authority on what is left.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose it and escape. This is a moment trophy: it needs the partner with you and the heat on, so do it when a mission or free-roam session already has you together — do not wait for a perfect moment that may not come again. Break line of sight, get out of the search area, and stay hidden until the stars clear. The description does not say whether the moment can be repeated, so treat it as do-it-when-it-comes and flag it in this guide as missable.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row without losing your wanted level. Back-to-back and unbroken is the whole challenge: plan a route past three shops, keep the pace up, and do not let the wanted level drop between robberies — if it clears, the chain breaks and you start again. Keep it quick and keep moving, and do it while your partner is with you. Flagged missable in this guide because it needs the partner moment; the description does not confirm whether it can be retried.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles (PSN tracks 0/100). Discovering means finding — driving past or getting into a new model — so the count grows fastest when you vary your rides: take a different car, bike, boat or plane whenever you travel instead of always grabbing the same one. The map is full of variety, so this climbs steadily on its own if you keep switching. The description does not list the vehicles, so the in-game collection is the source to check.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in one single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is the slow-time aiming mode: trigger it where enemies are grouped, and make every shot count before the meter runs out — five takedowns in one window is the bar. Pick a busy fight, wait until several enemies are in view, then activate it and work through them quickly. It can be retried in any shootout, so practise the timing on a replayable fight.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from VCIA, the Vice City airport. Read plainly, this is a stunt exit: leave the airport by air or by force rather than through the terminal — the word unscheduled is doing the work. Do it when you are already at the airport for the VCIA Takedown mission, while the layout is fresh in your mind. Flagged missable in this guide because it is a one-off moment at a specific place; the description does not confirm a retry, so take it when the chance comes.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The description is a joke with no instruction: 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos.' A Rhino is the series' tank, so this trophy is about the tanks — expect it to involve driving or fighting in one, and keep an eye out for Rhino encounters as you play. This guide does not invent the trigger: the official description does not state what to do, so the honest advice is to watch for tanks in missions and free roam and check the trophy the moment a Rhino appears. Flagged missable because a tank moment may only come once.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Stealth is the requirement: get in, take the goods and get out without any alarm or witness raising the heat — if you are spotted, back out and retry rather than fighting through it. Plan the approach first: case the store, enter quietly, and leave before anyone notices. Flagged missable in this guide because a botched silent run may not offer a clean second chance in the same moment; the description does not confirm a retry.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape (PSN tracks 0/5). Bank vaults are the big robberies: plan each one, crack the vault, and — the part the description stresses — escape afterwards, since the trophy counts the getaway as well as the robbery. Five vaults means five full jobs, so spread them across the late game when your crew and equipment are ready. The description does not name the five banks, so find them in-game and tick each off here.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks patrol the roads, so watch for one, stop it, take the cash and get away before the response arrives. The escape matters as much as the robbery — a clean getaway is what the trophy counts. Pick a quiet stretch of road away from police attention, hit the truck fast, and be gone before the wanted level builds.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida (PSN tracks 0/52). Leonida is the whole state — Vice City and everything around it — and the trophy wants every named area visited. Let it grow naturally as you play, then near the end open the map, find the areas you have never entered, and drive through each one. Pair it with WAiNK It locations and vehicle discovery, since all three reward covering the map. The description does not list the 52 areas, so the in-game map is the source.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs (PSN tracks 0/9). Every gang in Leonida runs operations you can hit — one per gang is the requirement, so keep a list of which gangs you have already robbed and which are still untouched. The description does not name the gangs or their operations, so scout them in-game and mark each gang off here as its operation falls.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. This is a quiet moment trophy: go to Ocean Beach, find a spot with a view — a bar or a beachfront seat — and have the cocktail. It is deliberately small after the heists and chases, so take it as a breather between bigger jobs. Flagged missable in this guide only because it asks for a specific place and moment; the description does not say the spot is one-time-only, so it should be repeatable — but do it the first time you are on Ocean Beach anyway.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. The classic style is the old GTA move: drive straight through the showroom glass and out the front. Find a showroom, get a car inside or lined up at the glass, and go through it in one run. Flagged missable because the moment is a single set-piece-style stunt; the description does not confirm whether a showroom can be smashed twice, so make the first attempt count.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. Go to that alley and bowl — follow-through is the bowling term for completing the throw, so play a full game and finish it properly rather than walking out mid-frame. The description names the alley, which is more than most trophies give, but does not say how many frames or games it takes, so play it through and watch for the pop. Flagged missable only as a specific-place moment; bowling itself should be repeatable.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: The description is deliberately vague — 'A partnership with mass appeal.' Partnership is the theme of the game's two leads, so this trophy is about something the pair does together that the public notices. This guide does not invent the trigger: no location or action is named, so the honest advice is to keep playing the story with both leads and watch for a partnership moment that draws a crowd. Flagged missable because a public moment may only happen once in the story.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Choices made, for better or worse — and PSN tracks a count to 500 (0/500), so this is a long tally of decisions, not a single choice. The game's story and side content keep offering choices; make them as they come and the count climbs. The number is large, so do not chase it directly: play normally, take every decision point you are offered, and check the counter late in the game. Flagged missable because a story choice, once made, may not be offered again — think before you pick at the big ones.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm.' The description says the trophy comes on a second attempt — something in the game that you fail once and then succeed at. The honest reading is that this is a retry trophy: the first failure is part of it, not a mistake. Do not fear failing the thing it refers to; the pop comes when the second try lands. This guide does not claim which attempt it is — the description names no event — so watch for a challenge or mission where a first failure is followed by a success, and flag it here when you find it.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: 'What the hell just happened?' Something strange happens — an event, a sighting, a surprise — and this trophy pops when you witness it. The description gives no location and no trigger, so this guide claims none: the honest advice is to explore, pay attention to odd sights and random events across Leonida, and keep this trophy in mind whenever something unusual happens. Flagged missable because a random or one-off event may not repeat.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by — knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. The bowling name is the joke: drive past a target, swing a melee weapon from the vehicle, and connect. Pick a slow drive-by on a lone pedestrian rather than a crowded street, and line the swing up before you reach them. Flagged missable as a specific-stunt moment; in practice drive-bys can be retried, so keep attempting it in free roam until it lands.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts (PSN tracks 0/250000). Marked Bills are dirty money from robberies that must be cleaned before they can be spent — take them to your contacts and launder them in batches. The total is large, so feed the system steadily: every robbery and vault job produces more bills, and the laundering total climbs with them. The description does not name the contacts or the rate, so use the in-game contacts to learn the flow.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops (PSN tracks 0/100000). This one takes care of itself if you play the game: weapons, clothes, cars, food and ammo all count, and a hundred thousand goes quickly once you start buying properly. Do not hoard cash for it — spend as you go, keep the good gear bought, and check the counter if it has not popped by the late game. It counts spending across all shops combined, so no single store matters.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties (PSN tracks 0/8). Garages are the properties that store your vehicle collection — buy every one the game offers, and this trophy pops on the last purchase. They cost money, so save for them across the mid-game rather than spending everything on cars first; the garages are what lets you keep the collection anyway. The description does not list the eight, so use the in-game property list and tick each purchase off here.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app (PSN tracks 0/10). Scooter Bros is the in-game vehicle app — open it, register the vehicles you own or find, and repeat until ten are on the books. It pairs with discovering vehicles for Whip It Good: every new vehicle you find is a candidate to register. The description does not say which vehicles qualify, so try the ones you own first and watch the counter.
trophies.name: On the Spot
